We are seeking a Senior Accounting Manager / Senior Accountant
to coordinate and support accounting and financial activities for the country. This role will be responsible for coordinating accounting projects, supporting financial close processes, ensuring compliance with internal controls and tax requirements, and partnering with different areas across the organization to support business initiatives and operational needs.
You will work closely with Accounting, Finance, Tax, IT, Operations, and other key stakeholders to ensure accurate, timely, and effective financial processes and reporting.

What's unique about this job (What you’ll do)

Accounting & Financial Operations

Coordinate accounting and financial processes for the country.
Support the timely and accurate completion of monthly, quarterly, and annual financial close processes.
Perform and oversee general ledger account reconciliations and follow up on outstanding items.
Prepare financial reports and monthly variance analyses.
Provide accounting information, reports, and documentation to Finance, Tax, Financial Reporting, and other teams as required.

Systems & Process Improvements

Support the implementation of new systems, processes, and business initiatives with accounting implications.
Serve as a key accounting user for systems such as JDE, TM1, and other financial platforms
.
Identify accounting and reporting requirements and coordinate solutions with IT and other functional areas.
Promote the development and use of system interfaces and process automation to improve efficiency and accuracy.

Internal Controls & Compliance

.
Follow up on local tax obligations and support the timely and accurate completion of monthly and annual tax requirements.
Identify opportunities to strengthen and automate accounting controls and processes.
Support inventory counts, cash/vault audits, and other control activities as required.

Business Partnership & Training

Partner with Operations, IT, Finance, Tax, and other teams to support business initiatives and provide accounting solutions.
Provide guidance and training to employees and users on accounting processes, systems, financial reporting, and best practices.
Maintain effective communication with accounting teams, Club management, and other stakeholders across the organization.
Support the implementation of new initiatives, clubs, procedures, and other business projects from an accounting perspective.

Bring your passion and expertise (Who you are)

Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Economics, Business Administration
, or a related field.
Solid experience in accounting and financial processes, including financial close, reconciliations, reporting, and variance analysis.
Experience coordinating accounting projects and working cross-functionally with different areas of an organization.
Strong technical knowledge and experience working with financial or accounting systems.
Experience with JDE is desirable
; knowledge of TM1 or similar financial reporting systems is a plus.
Knowledge of GAAP, SOX controls, internal controls, and local tax requirements
.
Excellent analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills.
Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work effectively with stakeholders at different levels of the organization.
Ability to prioritize multiple responsibilities and meet deadlines in a fast-paced environment.
Bilingual in English and Spanish.

Willingness to visit clubs, countries, or other locations when required to support business needs.

You feel connected to our mission and values: Integrity, Respect, Accountability, Passion, Community and Continuous Improvement.

Please protect your personal information during any recruitment process. While Monks may contact potential candidates via LinkedIn, all applications must be submitted through our official website (monks.com/careers).

R2R Regional Lead

Location: Hybrid, Bogotá, Colombia.

Monks Technology Services, part of Media.Monks and S4 Capital, is a global consulting firm mastering AI-powered transformations for the Fortune 100. We combine long-term strategic thinking, deep enterprise experience, and a human-centered approach to help clients transform business processes and dominate their industries.

As part of our commitment to inclusion and in compliance with Law 2466 of 2025 from Colombia, we have available spaces for people with disabilities.

About The Role

We are looking for an R2R Regional Lead based in Bogotá. You will report to local finance leadership and partner closely with Controllership teams to ensure that all deadlines are met in line with Group requirements. You will also act as R2R Global Process Owner (GPO), with a dual responsibility: driving global standardization and maintaining direct operational management for R2R activities within your assigned regions.

Responsibilities

Lead the R2R team operating on NetSuite OneWorld ERP to ensure timely completion of journal entries, revenue and balance sheet reconciliations, accruals, intercompany transactions, and fixed asset accounting, in line with Group month-end and reporting requirements.
Review and approve journal entries and balance sheet reconciliations, ensuring accounting entries are posted and approved in a timely manner by the R2R team.
Take full ownership of balance sheet accounts, perform analytical reviews, prepare and document month-end balance sheet specifications (reconciliations, GL account breakdowns, supporting documentation), and ensure appropriate actions are taken to resolve issues.
Review revenue recognition (e.g. net revenue, WIP).
Lead monthly balance sheet review meetings to ensure integrity, accuracy, and timely resolution of aging items.
Support both external and internal audits, providing evidential support and following up on action plans in case of deficiencies.
Manage the preparation of statutory financial statements in compliance with IFRS/GAAP and local requirements.
Ensure compliance with regional tax regulations (VAT/GST), data protection laws, and internal controls.
Act as primary point of contact for local statutory audits.

About You

Bachelor’s degree in Accounting or Finance, plus a fully qualified accounting designation (e.g. CPA, ACCA).
4+ years of accounting experience, specifically leading an R2R team within corporate finance structures or multi-entity environments.
Hands-on experience with NetSuite OneWorld, ideally including the Intercompany Management and Fixed Asset Management (FAM) modules.
Advanced Excel skills (pivot tables, VLOOKUPs) for data validation between NetSuite and external sources.
Strong knowledge of IFRS/GAAP and multi-currency environments (FX revaluation and translation).
English level: C1

At.Monks, we believe in fostering an environment where a diversity of perspectives can thrive. We proactively work to design hiring processes that promote equity and inclusion while mitigating bias. jobs.title: Accountant III
jobs.description:
Our team members are at the heart of everything we do. At Cencora, we are united in our responsibility to create healthier futures, and every person here is essential to us being able to deliver on that purpose. If you want to make a difference at the center of health, come join our innovative company and help us improve the lives of people and animals everywhere. Apply today!

Job Details

Summary Of Role

Under the direct supervision of the Regional Controller, the Accountant III is based in Bogotá, Colombia, and serves as the Regional Controller's primary right-hand resource for the North America region. This role combines strategic ownership of complex accounting matters with hands-on execution — including serving as the operational backup for the Accountant II across core transactional functions. Key responsibilities include owning complex reconciliations, policy research, and cross-functional coordination; acting as the principal liaison to Cencora's centralized AP shared services and Ariba procurement platform; providing technical review and guidance to the Accountant II; leading process documentation and improvement initiatives; collaborating with the World Courier Canada GL & Reporting Accountant to ensure the accuracy of Canadian financials and close activities; and supporting the upcoming SAP S/4HANA transition. All work is performed in English in support of US-based and Canadian entities, in accordance with US GAAP, SOX requirements, and internal company policies.

Responsabilities

Accounts Payable

Serve as the primary point of contact between the regional finance team and Cencora's centralized AP shared services organization; manage, track, and resolve AP escalations, vendor disputes, invoice discrepancies, and payment inquiries.
Act as the regional point person for SAP Ariba, supporting users with PO issues, invoice submission, requisition workflows, and escalations to the Ariba support team.
Ensure AP and Ariba processes are functioning accurately and in compliance with company policies; document recurring issues and recommend process improvements.

Financial Close & Reporting

Actively contribute to and help drive the monthly, quarterly, and annual US financial close process, including preparation and posting of journal entries, accruals, and adjusting entries, and stepping in to directly execute tasks as needed to meet close deadlines.
Prepare and review financial reporting packages and variance analyses for the North America region.
Lead preparation of audit schedules and manage responses to internal and external auditor requests for the region.
Own World Customs Brokerage (WCB) accounting end-to-end by developing a deep understanding of billing processes, workflows, and systems; ensuring all transactions are accurately journalized in SAP per US GAAP; reconciling balance sheet accounts monthly; and serving as the team's subject matter resource for WCB accounting questions.
Own World Courier Canada accounting end-to-end by collaborating with the local GL & Reporting Accountant to ensure accuracy and completeness of Canadian financials, balance sheet reconciliations, journal entries, and period-end close; and serving as the primary liaison between the Canada finance function and the Regional Controller for issue escalation and close status updates.

Accounting, Reconciliations & Documentation

Own and manage intercompany accounting processes across North America entities, including transaction recording, reconciliations, out-of-balance resolution, and coordination of intercompany eliminations during monthly close.
Serve as the subject matter resource for AR and intercompany accounting policy questions raised by the broader team.
Lead the preparation and review of high-complexity GL reconciliations, including those involving significant judgment, aged items, or cross-entity implications; research and resolve unusual reconciling items applying US GAAP and company policy.
Independently research accounting standards (ASC guidance, FASB updates, corporate policy changes) and present findings and recommended accounting treatment to the Regional Controller; assist with technical accounting memos as needed.
Lead the documentation of key accounting processes, procedures, and internal controls to ensure consistency, knowledge retention, and audit readiness; review and improve existing workpapers to reflect current processes.
Create and maintain standardized journal entry (JE) templates for recurring entries to reduce manual effort and improve accuracy; identify additional areas where templates or documented procedures can improve efficiency.

Review, Mentorship & Operational Backup of Accountant II

Own the technical review of journal entries, reconciliations, and financial reports prepared by the Accountant II, ensuring accuracy and compliance with US GAAP; provide real-time coaching and serve as the first point of escalation before items are elevated to the Regional Controller.
Maintain a thorough working knowledge of all Accountant II responsibilities — including journal entries, balance sheet and bank reconciliations, lease accounting (ASC 842), AP/AR support, and close checklist management — and step in to directly perform these tasks during absences, peak volume, or transitions.
Identify opportunities to cross-train and document Accountant II processes to reduce key-person risk and build organizational resilience.

General Responsibilities

Act as a trusted advisor and primary escalation resource for the Regional Controller on emerging accounting issues, policy questions, operational coverage needs, and ad hoc projects.
Communicate and collaborate daily with US-based employees via email, Microsoft Teams, and video calls — all conducted in English.
Identify opportunities to strengthen internal controls and improve accounting processes; ensure full compliance with SOX requirements, US GAAP, and Cencora corporate policies.
Maintain organized and accurate financial records and supporting documentation; complete all required training and stay current with changes to accounting standards.

Education

Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field.

Work Experience

Minimum of 6 years of directly related accounting experience (7–8 years preferred); experience supporting US-based or multinational operations strongly preferred.
4+ years of experience in accounting, financial reporting, close, or controllership activities required.
Strong working knowledge of US GAAP, preferred.
Proven experience managing or coordinating with AP shared services or centralized finance teams.
Excellent English proficiency (read, write, and communicate fluently).
Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel, including XLOOKUP, pivot tables, and complex formulas.
Experience with SAP or a comparable ERP system.

Skills And Knowledge

Advanced knowledge of Microsoft Excel, Word, PowerPoint, and Outlook.
Strong written and verbal communication skills in English.
Ability to work quickly and accurately under time and volume constraints, particularly during close periods.
Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities, with the ability to research and resolve complex issues with limited direction.
Demonstrated ability to review and provide constructive feedback on the work of peers.
Excellent organizational skills and meticulous attention to detail.
Ability to collaborate effectively in a remote, cross-border team environment.
Self-motivated with the ability to work independently and meet deadlines.

Work Environment

This role is based in Bogotá, Colombia, and supports US-based and Canadian operations. The associate will work during hours that overlap with US Eastern Time to facilitate real-time collaboration with US-based colleagues and Cencora's shared services team.

What Cencora offers

Benefit offerings outside the US may vary by country and will be aligned to local market practice. The eligibility and effective date may differ for some benefits and for team members covered under collective bargaining agreements.

Analizar, registrar y verificar provisiones y reclasificaciones contables dentro de los períodos de cierre.

Identificar, documentar y reportar riesgos y oportunidades fiscales para apoyar la toma de decisiones estratégicas.

Formación académica: Título profesional en Contaduría Pública.
Especialización: Posgrado o especialización en Tributación, Derecho Tributario o áreas afines.

Auditorías: Experiencia en preparación y acompañamiento de auditorías externas y corporativas.
Idioma inglés: Nivel avanzado de inglés (lectura, escritura y conversación).
Habilidades blandas: Capacidad de comunicación efectiva, trabajo colaborativo en equipo y habilidad para relacionarse transversalmente con diferentes áreas de la organización.

You’ll be responsible for consolidating, analyzing, and reviewing plant financial results, while supporting budgeting, forecasting, and strategic decision-making processes that enable sustainable business performance across the Pacific scope.

As a key Finance Business Partner, you will collaborate with plant leadership to provide insights, identify opportunities, validate financial decisions, and ensure compliance with financial controls. This role is based in Bogotá, Colombia.

Financial Planning & Forecasting: Lead the plant budgeting, forecasting, and annual operating plan processes, including standard cost budgeting and outlook preparation.
Business Partnering & Decision Support: Partner with plant leadership by conducting scenario analysis, identifying opportunity areas, and providing financial guidance to support business objectives.
Performance Analysis & Reporting: Consolidate plant financial results, analyze variances against targets, and prepare executive presentations for period-end, budget, and outlook reviews.
Cost Management & Controls: Monitor factory expenses, validate accruals, review budget parameters, and ensure compliance with internal audit and control requirements.
Capital & Continuous Improvement Initiatives: Evaluate investment opportunities, support ZBB compliance, and identify productivity and cost-saving opportunities to achieve financial targets.

We’re Looking for Someone With

Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, or a related field.
3+ years of experience in Supply Chain Finance, Manufacturing Finance, or Factory Finance environments.
Advanced Excel skills and experience with database management and SAP transactional analytics.
Business-level English proficiency with the ability to participate in professional and financial discussions.
Strong analytical, financial, and problem-solving capabilities with experience influencing stakeholders and driving business results.
Proven ability to prepare and deliver executive-level presentations and communications.
Demonstrated skills in strategic planning, business analytics, stakeholder management, and change management.

Worley is a global company of energy, chemicals and resources experts headquartered in Australia. We partner with our customers to deliver projects and create value across the life of their assets. Objective

THE PROJECT ACCOUNTANT II PROVIDES FINANCIAL GOVERNANCE AND CONTROL OVER PROJECTS THROUGHOUT THEIR LIFECYCLE BY LEADING PROJECT INCEPTION HANDOVERS, MONITORING COST AND REVENUE PERFORMANCE, AND ENSURING ACCURATE MONTH END REPORTING AND FORECASTING. Support new project setup and financial handover activities, ensuring accurate project structure, controls, and alignment with approved contractual and financial requirements.

Review and validate month‑end accruals, overhead allocations, and gross margin to ensure accurate and compliant project financial results.
Review and prepare actions of follow up related to cost rates, write‑offs, work in progress, billing in excess and revenue checklist.
Work collaboratively and in coordination with partners and the accounting outsourcing provider.

English proficiency at B1–B2 level.

Analizarás, estructurarás y comunicarás las implicaciones contable-tributarias de inversiones y estructuras patrimoniales de personas naturales y sociedades patrimoniales, mediante la aplicación de criterios técnicos, normativos y de análisis de información. El cargo tiene como propósito apoyar la construcción de soluciones patrimoniales para clientes de alto y ultra alto patrimonio mediante el análisis de tratamientos contables, obligaciones tributarias, efectos declarativos y diferencias entre bases contables y fiscales, facilitando la comprensión de estos temas por parte de clientes, banqueros privados y equipos internos.

Potenciarás las conversaciones y oportunidades comerciales con clientes UHNW dentro del proceso de planeación patrimonial del Grupo, analizando tu situación patrimonial nacional e internacional para aportar claridad técnica sobre los impactos contable-tributarios de sus estructuras y operaciones bajo normas locales e internacionales (IFRS, US GAAP). Monitorearás cambios en la normativa y en los criterios contables relevantes para las inversiones de personas naturales, sociedades patrimoniales y la estructuración u originación de productos, con el fin de elaborar insumos técnicos oportunos, anticiparás impactos y mantendrás actualizados a los equipos internos que participan en la narrativa comercial y en los procesos de venta.

jobs.title: Consultor Senior de Transformación Contable y Financiera (RTR)
jobs.description:
Accenture es una compañía global líder en servicios profesionales con una amplia gama de soluciones en estrategia y consultoría, tecnología y operaciones, capacidades digitales, brindando un servicio integral a nuestros clientes para que alcancen su máximo rendimiento.

El Global Process Owner (GPO) de RTR es el máximo responsable del diseño, gobernanza y evolución continua del proceso de extremo a extremo de Record to Report a nivel global. Este rol lidera la transformación del ciclo contable desde una perspectiva de reingeniería profunda, impulsando la automatización, la estandarización y la adopción de mejores prácticas que generen eficiencia operativa y visibilidad financiera en tiempo real para toda la organización.

El puesto requiere analizar y resolver problemas de complejidad moderada y, a menudo, crear nuevas soluciones aprovechando o adaptando métodos y procedimientos existentes. El GPO de RTR actúa como catalizador de este cambio: cuestiona el status quo, diseña el proceso futuro ("to-be") con visión digital y colabora con tecnología, operaciones, auditoría y liderazgo senior para asegurar que cada mejora esté anclada en valor de negocio medible. No gestiona el proceso —lo diseña, lo gobierna y lo mejora sin parar.

Responsabilidades principales:

Transformación y Reingeniería de Procesos

Liderar el rediseño end-to-end del proceso RTR (contabilidad, impuestos y FPnA) con enfoque en eliminación de desperdicios, reducción de ciclos y maximización del valor.

Definir el modelo "to-be" del proceso contable.

Conducir talleres de diagnóstico (process mining, value stream mapping) para identificar cuellos de botella y oportunidades de mejora.

Impulsar iniciativas de simplificación estructural: reducción de entidades legales, consolidación de chart of accounts, armonización de calendarios de cierre.

Automatización y Digitalización Contable

Definir la hoja de ruta de automatización del ciclo contable: desde la generación de asientos automáticos hasta el reporte financiero.

Liderar la implementación de tecnologías de automatización en el proceso RTR.

Establecer la visión de "Continuous Accounting" como modelo operativo objetivo, eliminando el pico de trabajo del cierre mensual.

Estandarización y Gobernanza Global

Diseñar y mantener el marco de procesos estándar RTR: políticas, procedimientos, controles, roles y responsabilidades (RACI global).

Gestionar la biblioteca de procesos (process repository) y asegurar su actualización permanente.

Establecer un modelo de gobernanza con foros de proceso, KPIs de desempeño y mecanismos de excepción controlada.

Asegurar el cumplimiento de controles y regulaciones locales dentro del diseño del proceso.

Definir y monitorear métricas clave del proceso

Gestión de Tecnología y Sistemas

Actuar como puente entre Finanzas y TI/Tecnología para asegurar que los sistemas soporten el diseño del proceso y no al revés.

Liderar el proceso de validación y UAT de cambios tecnológicos que impactan el ciclo RTR.

Evaluar continuamente el landscape tecnológico del mercado e identificar herramientas que aceleren la transformación.

Colaboración Interfuncional

Articular el proceso RTR con los procesos upstream (P2P, O2C) y downstream (Tesorería, Auditoría).

Colaborar con los GPOs de otros procesos para garantizar integración y coherencia en el modelo operativo financiero global.

Lo que necesitas para postularte:

Mínimo 7 años de experiencia similar.

Competencias técnicas específicas: Visión de Negocios, Contabilidad de costos

Educación superior completa preferiblemente Ciencias Contables, Finanzas, Dirección de Empresas o Administración de Empresas. Los estudios de posgrado se considerarán un diferencial.

Gestión y liderazgo de personas.

Inglés avanzado.

Excel avanzado.

Todas las decisiones de Accenture se tomarán sin discriminar por motivos de raza, religión, color, sexo, edad, discapacidad, nacionalidad, orientación sexual, identidad o expresión de género, ni por ninguna otra razón cubierta por la legislación local.

jobs.title: Senior Project Controller
jobs.description:
Role Summary

WSP is seeking a Project Controller to join the Québec Buildings Team (ST-CI & M&E), providing financial and administrative support to Project Managers while contributing to the successful delivery of building projects. Reporting to the Operations Coordinator, the successful candidate will play a key role in ensuring effective coordination between Operations, Finance, Accounting, Billing, and Accounts Receivable teams. This position is critical to maintaining financial integrity, supporting project performance, and contributing to projects that help shape the future of our communities.

Responsibilities

Provide support to the Project Management Office (PMO) in the use and administration of Oracle, including project setup, project modifications, and baseline resets.
Ensure the accuracy, creation, maintenance, quality and ongoing updates of project-related data, including opportunities, projects, budgets, and revenue information, within corporate systems.
Identify variances between project costs and revenues and coordinate the implementation of corrective actions with relevant stakeholders.
Prepare and maintain periodic project forecasts, including Estimate at Completion (EAC) and Estimate to Complete (ETC), in collaboration with Project Managers and Project Directors.
Support Project Managers with financial and project control activities, complementing the work performed by Project Accountants and Finance teams.
Participate in project change management processes and ensure proper financial impacts are reflected.
Facilitate effective coordination between Operations, Finance, Billing, and other project stakeholders.
Improve the flow, accessibility, and understanding of project financial information, serving as a key resource for project teams.
Monitor project financial performance and prepare reports to support informed decision-making.
Contribute to the successful achievement of project financial and operational objectives.
Lead meetings between Project Managers and Project Directors to request and gather updated information on project status, financial performance, forecasts, and key changes.

Competencies / Skills / Qualifications

Technical Diploma, associate degree, bachelor’s degree, or equivalent qualification in Business Administration, Accounting, Finance, Engineering, Project Management, or related field.
Additional education or certifications in Project Controls, Financial Management, Project Management, or related disciplines will be considered an asset.
Any equivalent combination of education and relevant experience will be considered.
6-9 years of experience in Project Controls, Project Financial Management, Cost Control, or Project Administration.
Understanding within the buildings, engineering, infrastructure, or construction industries.
Strong experience in project budgeting, forecasting, cost control, variance analysis, and financial performance monitoring.
Experience working with multidisciplinary teams and multiple stakeholders.
Solid knowledge of Project Controls principles and methodologies.
Experience with Earned Value Management (EVM).
Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel.
Experience with ERP systems, preferably Oracle.
Experience preparing and managing EAC (Estimate at Completion) and ETC (Estimate to Complete) forecasts.
Strong analytical and financial reporting capabilities.
Analytical thinking.
Attention to detail.
Results-oriented mindset.
Teamwork and collaboration.
Strong communication skills.
Planning and organizational skills.
Proactive and self-motivated approach.
Ability to manage multiple priorities.
Autonomy and commitment to quality work.
Dynamic and positive attitude.
Advanced English proficiency, both written and spoken.
French, both written and spoken is an asset
Any equivalent combination of education, experience, and qualifications demonstrating the ability to successfully perform the responsibilities of the role will be considered.

Iron Mountain is seeking a commercially-driven and detail-oriented Senior Deal Modeler & Pricing Analyst to join our Digital Business Unit (DBU) Americas team.

In this role, you’ll play a key part in translating technical architecture into competitive pricing structures that drive our digital transformation efforts forward.
You will have the opportunity to independently build financial models and margin analyses
, ensuring our custom digital solutions are priced efficiently and sustainably. Here, your expertise will help evaluate complex deal economics and shape the strategic direction of our rapidly growing digital service offerings.

What You’ll Do

In this role, you will:

Build Deal-Level Pricing Models: Translate technical solution inputs and operational estimates into accurate financial models and line-item margin analyses.
Prepare Executive Presentations: Craft clear pricing summaries, sensitivity charts, and presentation decks to outline deal economics and recommend structures for leadership review.
Perform Scenario Modeling: Conduct financial sensitivity analyses, break-even calculations, and triage incoming deal requests against intake criteria.
Apply Cost Benchmarks: Utilize established Cost Master metrics for labor, equipment, and facility overhead to ensure custom deal builds and Change Requests are priced effectively.
Analyze Performance Metrics: Monitor discounting trends, concession logs, and operational throughput to identify systemic opportunities for margin and price growth.

What You’ll Bring

The ideal candidate will have:

5+ years of experience in Strategic Pricing, or Deal Desk within digital services, B2B, tech and complex multinational matrix environments.
Strong knowledge of SaaS business environments and advanced Sheets financial modeling and evaluating complex technical solution scopes or capital investments.
Proven ability to translate intricate data into clear, actionable insights using professional presentation tools (e.g., G Suite / Slides) for non-finance stakeholders.
Demonstrated capability to independently lead deal modeling for multi-variable opportunities with minimal supervisory oversight.
A Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, or Economics and fluent in English and Spanish. Portuguese is a plus. (please submit your cv in English).

What We Offer

Working from Home Model (based in Colombia or Mexico)
Competitive compensation and benefits aligned with experience.
Opportunities for continuous learning and professional growth in a global environment.

Ready to take the next step and help shape the future of our digital solutions? Apply today to join our team.

jobs.description:
Accounting Data Analyst — Revenue

As one of the top mobility companies in the world, we have been redefining the industry with innovative mobile technologies since 2013, driving us toward becoming a super app. Join us in our mission to combat global injustice.

We are looking for an experienced accounting professional with strong technical and data skills to join our global Accounting team. In this role, you'll prepare journal entries, account reconciliations, and revenue data packages that keep our books accurate, auditable, and US GAAP compliant — while writing the SQL and building the automation that makes those processes scalable as we prepare for public company readiness.
You'll report to a US-based Revenue Accounting leader and partner daily with accounting, data, and payment reconciliation colleagues across the globe. This is a hands-on role for someone who is equally comfortable posting a journal entry in an ERP and querying a data warehouse — and who gets energized by fixing broken processes, not just running them.

What You'll Do

Prepare complete, review-ready journal entries across revenue, accounts receivable, payment provider settlements, chargebacks/refunds, taxes, and intercompany — with full supporting detail for ERP posting
Prepare account reconciliations, flux analyses, and supporting schedules for monthly, quarterly, and annual close
Write and maintain SQL queries against our data warehouse to extract and validate the data behind accruals and ASC 606 revenue recognition
Support payment service provider (PSP) reconciliations — validating settlement, refund, chargeback, and fee data across geographies and currencies, and flagging discrepancies
Document processes end-to-end and support SOX readiness, responding to internal and external audit requests as the preparer with full traceability from source to output
Identify manual, error-prone steps and automate them — including with AI-enabled tooling — partnering with Data Engineering, IT, and FinTech teams

What We're Looking For

~8 years of progressive accounting experience, including hands-on journal entry preparation and month-end close ownership
Accounting degree with CRC or equivalent professional qualification (CPA-equivalent)
Solid working knowledge of US GAAP; hands-on ASC 606 revenue recognition experience is a major plus
Strong SQL skills — able to write and adapt queries against large-scale data warehouses (BigQuery or similar)
Proficiency with an ERP system (NetSuite, SAP, Oracle or similar): chart of accounts, journal entry posting, validation, and drill-down analysis
Experience supporting internal or external audits; exposure to SOX controls and documentation
Fluent English — this role works daily with a US-based team during Eastern Time hours

Nice to Have

Big 4 or large multinational (Fortune 500-scale) background; IPO or public company readiness experience
Industry experience with complex, high-volume revenue models (tech/marketplace, retail, media, manufacturing)
Experience with data visualization tools (Power BI, Tableau) and scripting for automation

Who Thrives Here

Someone gritty and curious who gets into the weeds, asks questions, and comes with proposed solutions. We're moving fast toward a bigger goal: priorities pivot, hours can stretch during peak periods, and feedback is direct. If you like ambiguity, ownership, and building processes that didn't exist yesterday, you'll fit right in!

What we offer

Competitive compensation package
Comprehensive medical insurance coverage.
Meal allowance
Dental Insurance
Hybrid setting
Opportunity for advancement and upward mobility within the organization, allowing for increased levels of responsibility and growth within the company

jobs.title: Controller
jobs.description:
We are one of the largest and fastest growing private youth sports operators in the GTA. We provide fun, engaging experiences, creating lasting memories for the youth and families in our communities!

We're looking for a detail-oriented, hands-on Controller to lead our day-to-day accounting operations and help ensure the financial health and integrity of our organization as we continue to grow. As Controller, you will own the accounting function end to end — from monthly close and financial reporting to internal controls and compliance. You'll work closely with the financial team to provide accurate, timely financial information that supports sound decision-making across the organization. This is a great opportunity for an experienced accounting professional who enjoys both the technical rigor of the numbers and the process-improvement side of the role.

Responsibilities

Perform full-cycle bookkeeping duties, including accounts payable, accounts receivable, payroll, and bank reconciliations
Match bank feeds and reconcile accounts in QuickBooks Online, including inter-company bookkeeping across related entities
Manage AR (invoicing and payment processing) and AP (vendor correspondence and scheduling timely payments) -
Process semi-monthly payroll using Wagepoint and Square
Apply knowledge of HST and Input Tax Credits to ensure accurate tax filings and remittances
Review and authorize staff expense reimbursements
Manage the monthly, quarterly, and annual close process and provide financial reporting, including P&L, balance sheet, and cash flow statements
Develop and maintain internal controls and accounting policies to ensure GAAP compliance, and coordinate annual audits, tax filings, and regulatory reporting requirements
Prepare budget-to-actual variance analyses and support annual budgeting and forecasting
Maintain proficiency in QuickBooks Online and Excel, bringing a detail-oriented, organized approach to all financial record-keeping
Partner with the CFO and department leaders through professional correspondence and team coordination, and identify opportunities to streamline accounting processes

Requirements

Strong knowledge of GAAP and financial reporting standards
Proficiency with accounting software and advanced Excel skills; experience with ERP or cloud-based accounting platforms is a plus
Excellent analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills
Strong communication skills, with the ability to translate financial data into clear insights for non-finance stakeholders
High degree of accuracy, integrity, and attention to detail
Ability to work independently in a remote environment while collaborating effectively with a distributed team
Experience in the sports, nonprofit, or membership-based organization sector is a plus, but not required
Complete both of our short assessments (about 5 minutes each) before or right after applying. Applications with both completed are reviewed first:
Culture Index survey
Skills game assessment

Benefits

new_jobs.title: Senior Accounts Payable Specialist
new_jobs.description:
Accounting, Accounting & Finance, Accounts Payable, Financial Operations

About The Position

Royal York Property Management is seeking a highly experienced Senior Accounts Payable Specialist to support the accuracy, organization, and control of our accounts payable operations.

This position will play an important role in ensuring invoices are properly reviewed, expenses are accurately recorded, vendor accounts remain current, and payment requests are complete and ready for approval. The successful candidate will work closely with members of our finance, property management, maintenance, and operations teams.

We are looking for someone who understands the complete accounts payable cycle and can manage their responsibilities with limited supervision. This is not a junior invoice-entry position. The person hired must be capable of identifying irregularities, investigating discrepancies, maintaining reliable records, and protecting the integrity of the company’s payment processes.

Previous experience supporting Canadian companies is required. Candidates should already be comfortable working with Canadian invoices, GST and HST coding, Canadian vendors, and Ontario-based team members.

Our Hiring Process

Every application is reviewed by our recruitment team.

Candidates whose education and experience appear to align with the position will receive an email within one to two business days of applying with a link to complete a pre-recorded online interview.

The interview allows us to evaluate your accounts payable experience, Canadian-company exposure, technical knowledge, judgment, communication skills, and ability to manage senior-level responsibilities in a remote environment.

Only candidates selected to move forward will be contacted regarding the next stage of the hiring process.

Key Responsibilities

Review invoices for accuracy, completeness, supporting documentation, and proper authorization
Code and enter invoices using the correct company, department, account, tax treatment, and cost allocation
Match invoices to purchase orders, work orders, contracts, service records, and other supporting documents
Manage vendor records, payment terms, contact information, and banking details
Prepare payment batches and supporting schedules for management review and approval
Reconcile vendor statements and investigate differences between vendor records and the accounting system
Resolve missing invoices, duplicate billings, unapplied credits, incorrect balances, and payment discrepancies
Monitor due dates, overdue balances, payment commitments, and upcoming cash requirements
Respond to vendor inquiries regarding invoice status, account balances, and payment timing
Process credit-card transactions, employee expenses, recurring charges, and other operating expenses
Apply the appropriate GST and HST treatment to invoices and expenses
Assist with accounts payable, bank, and credit-card reconciliations
Support month-end activities, including accruals, cut-off procedures, prepaid expenses, and outstanding invoice reviews
Maintain complete and well-organized electronic records for review and audit purposes
Support accounts payable activities involving multiple entities, departments, properties, and vendor relationships
Identify process gaps, control weaknesses, and recurring errors
Recommend practical improvements to increase accuracy, efficiency, and accountability
Follow approval limits, segregation-of-duties requirements, and fraud-prevention procedures
Collaborate with internal departments to obtain missing information and resolve payment-related issues

Education And Experience Requirements

Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration with an accounting concentration, or a closely related field
Colombian Contador Público qualification or another relevant accounting designation is considered an asset but is not mandatory
Minimum 4 years of directly related accounts payable or accounting operations experience
Candidates with 4–7+ years of relevant experience are strongly preferred
Previous experience supporting one or more Canadian companies is required
Demonstrated experience managing the full accounts payable cycle
Experience reviewing, coding, processing, and reconciling a high volume of invoices
Practical knowledge of Canadian GST and HST coding
Experience preparing payment runs or payment batches for approval
Strong vendor statement reconciliation and discrepancy-resolution skills
Experience supporting month-end closing activities
Experience working with multiple companies, entities, departments, or cost centres
Property management, real estate, construction, maintenance, or service-industry accounting experience is considered an asset
Strong proficiency with Microsoft Excel or Google Sheets
Experience with QuickBooks Online or another established accounting or ERP platform
Advanced written and spoken English
Confidence communicating with vendors, managers, and cross-functional team members
Ability to work full-time during Ontario business hours
Reliable computer, high-speed internet connection, headset, webcam, and quiet professional workspace

The Person We Are Looking For

You are a careful and experienced accounting professional who understands the responsibility involved in handling company expenses and vendor payments.

You do not process information blindly. You verify documentation, question inconsistencies, investigate unusual activity, and follow issues through to resolution.

You are comfortable managing deadlines, communicating with multiple departments, and balancing speed with accuracy. You understand when an issue can be resolved independently and when it must be documented and escalated.

You also recognize that strong accounts payable performance depends on sound controls, reliable records, professional communication, and consistent follow-through.

Measures of Success

Success In This Role Means

Invoices are processed accurately and within the required timelines
Expenses are assigned to the correct accounts, entities, and cost centres
Taxes are coded correctly
Vendor balances are regularly reconciled and supported
Payment batches are accurate, complete, and ready for approval
Duplicate, unsupported, or unauthorized payments are identified before funds are released
Outstanding issues are documented and followed through to completion
Vendor communications are handled professionally
Month-end information is accurate and delivered on time
Accounts payable records are complete, organized, and review-ready
Management has dependable information regarding payment obligations and outstanding balances

Compensation

The annual compensation range for this position is:

C$27,600–C$32,400

Final compensation will be determined based on the candidate’s depth of accounts payable experience, previous work with Canadian companies, knowledge of Canadian tax coding, accounting-system proficiency, industry exposure, English communication skills, and ability to independently manage complex accounts payable responsibilities.

new_jobs.title: Senior Accounts Receivable & Collections Specialist
new_jobs.description:
Accounting, Accounting & Finance, Accounts Receivable, Billing, Cash Application, Collections, Collections Operations, Credit & Collections, Financial Operations

Hours:
Full-Time, aligned with EST business hours

The Opportunity

Royal York Property Management is seeking an experienced receivables professional to oversee customer account accuracy, overdue balance recovery, payment follow-up, and collection reporting.

This position combines financial administration with direct customer communication. The person hired will be expected to maintain reliable account records while actively moving unpaid balances toward resolution.

You must be able to determine why an account remains unpaid, distinguish between billing problems and genuine collection risk, coordinate with internal departments, and take appropriate action without constant supervision.

This is a senior individual-contributor position. It is not intended for someone whose experience is primarily limited to issuing invoices, posting receipts, or sending standard payment reminders.

Previous Experience Supporting Canadian Companies Is Required.

Professional Profile

You are persistent without being unnecessarily aggressive.

You can protect a professional customer relationship while remaining direct about payment obligations, deadlines, and missed commitments.

You understand the difference between a customer who has a legitimate dispute, a customer experiencing financial difficulty, and a customer who is avoiding payment.

You keep accurate notes, follow through consistently, and know when an account requires escalation.

Most importantly, you are comfortable being accountable for actual collection outcomes rather than simply the number of calls or emails completed.

Core Responsibilities

Collections and Account Recovery

Contact customers by telephone and email regarding outstanding balances
Manage follow-up across current, 30-, 60-, and 90-day receivables
Prioritize accounts based on age, value, payment history, dispute status, and recovery risk
Obtain and document payment dates, commitments, and required next steps
Follow up promptly when payment commitments are missed
Discuss payment arrangements that fall within approved company policies
Investigate whether non-payment results from a billing issue, service concern, administrative delay, or financial difficulty
Escalate high-value, disputed, severely overdue, or high-risk accounts
Coordinate with internal teams to resolve legitimate account issues
Identify balances that may require legal review, service restrictions, external collections, settlement consideration, or write-off review
Prepare collection forecasts and report expected and uncertain cash receipts
Recommend improvements to reminder timing, escalation procedures, documentation standards, and account-risk management

Accounts Receivable Administration

Maintain accurate customer balances, account histories, and billing records
Review billing information before invoices and statements are issued
Apply incoming payments to the correct customer, invoice, and legal entity
Resolve unapplied receipts, deductions, short payments, credits, refunds, and overpayments
Reconcile customer accounts and correct identified differences
Maintain current billing contacts, payment terms, customer notes, and supporting records
Review aging reports and identify accounts requiring action
Support accounts receivable reconciliations, reporting, and month-end close
Work across multiple companies, legal entities, departments, and customer portfolios
Coordinate with finance and operational teams when accounting records do not match the underlying agreement or service history
Maintain complete, organized, and review-ready documentation

Required Background

Minimum 4 years of directly relevant accounts receivable, collections, credit, billing, or accounting operations experience
Candidates with 4–7+ years of relevant experience are strongly preferred
Previous experience supporting Canadian companies is required
Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration with an accounting concentration, or a closely related discipline
A recognized professional accounting designation is considered an asset but is not mandatory
Demonstrated experience managing both accounts receivable administration and active collections
Experience carrying responsibility for an assigned customer portfolio
Direct experience conducting telephone and email collections
Experience reviewing aging reports and managing delinquent balances
Strong customer-account reconciliation and discrepancy-resolution skills
Experience applying payments and resolving unapplied cash
Experience handling billing disputes, deductions, credits, short payments, refunds, and overpayments
Experience documenting and monitoring payment commitments
Experience negotiating payment schedules within approved guidelines
Experience preparing collection forecasts, aging summaries, or expected cash-receipt reports
Experience contributing to month-end accounting activities
Strong Excel or Google Sheets capability
Experience with QuickBooks Online or another established accounting or ERP platform
Advanced spoken and written English
Ability to communicate clearly and remain composed during difficult collection conversations
Ability to work full-time during Ontario business hours
Reliable computer equipment, high-speed internet, headset, webcam, and a quiet professional workspace

Experience in property management, real estate, leasing, construction, maintenance, financial services, or another service-based environment is considered beneficial.

Application and Interview Process

Applications are assessed against the education, experience, communication, and technical requirements of the role.

Candidates selected for initial screening will receive an email within one to two business days of applying with a link to complete a pre-recorded interview.

The interview will evaluate Canadian-company experience, accounts receivable knowledge, collections judgment, customer communication, systems experience, and the ability to manage difficult accounts independently.

Candidates who meet the required standard may be invited to a live interview.

Performance Expectations

The Successful Candidate Will Be Expected To

Reduce aged receivables, particularly balances exceeding 60 and 90 days
Maintain complete and useful customer account notes
Apply incoming payments promptly and accurately
Produce reliable collection and cash-receipt forecasts
Resolve billing disputes and account discrepancies efficiently
Maintain consistent contact with overdue customers
Monitor and follow up on broken payment commitments
Keep customer balances accurate and reconciled
Escalate high-risk balances before recovery becomes unlikely
Reduce unresolved unapplied cash
Follow company approval limits and financial controls
Maintain professional, direct, and well-documented customer communication
Avoid unauthorized settlements, reductions, refunds, waivers, or write-offs

Scope of Authority

The specialist may discuss payment timing and establish arrangements that remain within approved company guidelines.

Management Authorization Is Required Before

Approving an arrangement outside established limits
Reducing or settling a valid account balance
Referring an account to an external collection agency
Waiving material charges or interest
Suspending services
Writing off an amount owed
Referring an account to legal counsel

The specialist must investigate the account, document the circumstances, and present a clear recommendation before seeking approval.

Compensation and Bonus

Base Compensation For This Position Is

C$30,000–C$40,000 annually

The Role Also Offers

Up to C$4,800 annually in quarterly performance-based bonus potential

The Maximum Quarterly Bonus Is

C$1,200

Performance May Be Assessed Using Factors Such As

Accuracy of cash-receipt forecasts
Reduction in 60- and 90-day receivables
Timely escalation of high-risk accounts
Percentage of customer payment commitments received as promised
Quality and completeness of account documentation
Collection results across assigned accounts
Compliance with approval limits and internal controls
Accuracy of payment application and customer reconciliations
Speed and quality of dispute resolution
Professional quality of customer communication

Final compensation will be based on the candidate’s relevant experience, Canadian-company background, collections performance, portfolio complexity, systems knowledge, communication ability, and capacity to work independently.

new_jobs.title: Analista contable
new_jobs.description:
Buscamos un Contador detallista y analítico para gestionar todas las transacciones financieras de nuestra organización. Tu misión principal será garantizar que los estados financieros sean precisos, que el pago de impuestos se realice en tiempo y forma, y que la empresa cumpla rigurosamente con la normativa contable y fiscal vigente. Serás una pieza clave para la toma de decisiones estratégicas basadas en datos financieros reales.

Responsabilidades principales

Gestión del Ciclo Contable: Registrar y supervisar las operaciones diarias (asientos contables, cuentas por cobrar/pagar, activos fijos).

Elaboración de Estados Financieros: Preparar balances generales, estados de resultados y flujos de efectivo mensuales y anuales.

Cumplimiento Fiscal: Calcular y presentar declaraciones de impuestos (IVA, IRPF, Impuesto sobre Sociedades, etc.) de acuerdo con la legislación local.

Conciliaciones Bancarias: Asegurar que los registros internos coincidan con los estados de cuenta bancarios de forma regular.

Gestión de Nóminas y Proveedores: Supervisar el pago a empleados y la correcta facturación y liquidación de proveedores.

Auditoría Interna: Preparar la documentación necesaria para auditorías externas y asegurar el cumplimiento de los controles internos.

Análisis de Costos: Realizar análisis de desviaciones presupuestarias y proponer medidas de ahorro o eficiencia.

Requisitos y Cualificaciones

Formación: Grado o Licenciatura en Contaduría Pública Experiencia: Mínimo de 1 a 2 años en puestos contables similares.

Conocimientos Técnicos: Profundo dominio de las Normas Internacionales de Información Financiera (NIIF/IFRS) y de la legislación tributaria local.

Atención al Detalle: Capacidad para identificar discrepancias mínimas en grandes volúmenes de datos.

Integridad y Ética: Manejo de información sensible con absoluta confidencialidad y honestidad.

Pensamiento Analítico: Habilidad para interpretar lo que los números dicen sobre el negocio.

Contrato directo con la compañía, Lunes y martes de 6:00 a.m. a 4:00 p.m.; miércoles y jueves de 6:30 a.m. a 4:00 p.m.; viernes de 7:00 a.m. a 3:00 p.m.

Project Accountant

Role Summary

The Project Accountant role provides financial support and advisory to the Project Manager. This is a role that reports to a financial function, typically to a Financial Controller, and is typically budgeted in the overhead costs of a project. This role is assigned to multiple projects.

Responsibilities

Set up project in financial systems including project funding, revenue recognition, bill plans, contract overrides and billing/revenue controls.
Provide project pricing support (bill rates, contract overhead allowance, etc.).
Support/review project setup and change orders in financial system (WBS, budgets, margin expectations, and contingency/reserves).
Provide contractual and client compliance support including maintaining certificates of insurance, subcontractor/DBE reporting, rate/per diem caps, and identifying unallowable costs.
Ensure project financials are accurately reported in line with the Project’s commercial authorization.
Support financial performance of the project through monitoring project costs and recognized revenue (including calculating labour breakage/enhancements, overruns, missing bill/revenue rates, etc.).
Support project team in monthly reviews from a financial perspective, including estimated gains/losses.
Support DSO and collection efforts through monitoring unbilled costs, WIP, and AR in accordance to the terms and conditions of its contract, as approved by the project manager.
Be responsible for reconciliation of project financials at closeout.
Perform weekly reconciliation of labour hours, project charges, and financial transactions between BST (Colombia) and Horizon (Canada/US) to ensure completeness, accuracy, and timely correction of variances.
Support and monitor BST-Horizon project integration, including project setup validation, mapping of project structures, charge codes, and ongoing data integrity between systems.
Produce and distribute a weekly exception report identifying missed transactions, interface failures, unmatched labour postings, billing discrepancies, and other data quality issues requiring corrective action.
Coordinate with project managers, operations teams, and finance stakeholders to resolve cross-system discrepancies and ensure project financial data is current and accurate.
Maintain oversight of project and employee charging compliance by proactively identifying and resolving missing timesheets, incorrect project allocations, and unposted transactions.
Support month-end close activities through verification of BST-Horizon reconciliation, resolution of outstanding exceptions, and confirmation of project financial accuracy prior to invoicing and reporting.
Support Horizon implementation and post-go-live stabilization activities in GCC Colombia, including data migration validation, project and employee master data setup, timesheet compliance monitoring, user support, reconciliation of migrated transactions, and resolution of issues impacting project financial reporting and labour charging accuracy.

Description

The Financial Analyst - CS GO Finance will drive cost efficiency and operational excellence for Amazon's Customer Service organization by leading financial analysis for VCPC (Variable Cost Per Contact) projects and strategic initiatives. This role partners with CS GO and cross-functional teams globally to identify optimization opportunities, analyze cost trends, and deliver year-over-year improvements. The ideal candidate combines strong financial acumen with the ability to translate complex data into actionable insights that enable leadership to make informed decisions and achieve key business goals with a high bar for cost efficiency.

Key job responsibilities

As a Financial Analyst supporting VCPC (Variable Cost Per Contact) initiatives, you will:

Lead financial analysis for VCPC improvement projects, identifying cost reduction opportunities and efficiency gains across Customer Service operations

Partner with cross-functional stakeholders to influence decision-making on cost optimization initiatives and resource allocation

Track and report on project performance, monitoring key metrics and providing regular updates on progress toward YoY improvement targets

Analyze cost trends by month, location, and vertical to identify optimization opportunities and support data-driven recommendations

Develop financial models and business cases to evaluate VCPC initiatives and quantify potential savings

Support monthly and quarterly financial reporting, providing insights into variances and trends that impact VCPC performance

Collaborate with Customer Service, Operations, and Finance teams to ensure alignment on project goals and deliverables

Communicate findings clearly to stakeholders at various levels, translating complex financial data into actionable insights

Build and maintain tracking mechanisms to measure the impact of improvement initiatives and ensure accountability for results

A day in the life

You'll start your day reviewing VCPC performance metrics and identifying trends that require deeper analysis. You'll collaborate with Customer Service and Operations leaders to discuss ongoing cost optimization projects, providing financial insights that guide decision-making. Much of your time will be spent building financial models, analyzing cost drivers across different locations and verticals, and tracking progress on improvement initiatives. You'll prepare updates for stakeholders, clearly communicating project status and financial impact. You'll also participate in cross-functional meetings to influence resource allocation decisions and ensure alignment on YoY improvement targets.

Job Description

Futura USA Inc. is seeking a highly organized and detail-oriented Construction Accounting Manager
to oversee the day-to-day financial and accounting processes of our construction operations. This role will be responsible for ensuring accurate project billing, collections, payments, payroll coordination, job costing, and financial reporting across multiple active projects.
The ideal candidate has experience in construction accounting and understands progress billing, retainage, change orders, subcontractor/vendor payments, project costs, and cash flow.
Responsibilities

Prepare and send client invoices based on project billing schedules, milestones, and approved change orders
Manage accounts receivable and actively follow up on outstanding payments
Process and track vendor and subcontractor invoices
Manage accounts payable and prepare payments for approval
Coordinate and maintain payroll, contractor payments, reimbursements, and related records
Maintain accurate job costing for labor, materials, subcontractors, equipment, freight, and other project expenses
Track deposits, retainage, stored materials, progress billings, and change orders
Reconcile bank accounts, credit cards, and financial transactions
Maintain accurate project financial information in QuickBooks and company management software
Ensure all transactions are properly categorized by project and cost code
Maintain WIP schedules and monitor project profitability
Prepare weekly cash flow, accounts receivable, accounts payable, and upcoming payment reports
Assist management with monthly P&L, balance sheet, project profitability, and financial reporting
Coordinate with project managers to ensure billing milestones are invoiced promptly
Maintain organized financial documentation for projects, vendors, subcontractors, and clients
Coordinate with the company’s CPA and outside accounting professionals as needed
Help establish and maintain strong financial controls and accounting procedures

Qualifications

3+ years of accounting or finance experience, preferably within the construction industry
Strong understanding of construction accounting, job costing, progress billing, retainage, A/R, and A/P
Experience with QuickBooks Online or similar accounting software
Experience processing or coordinating payroll
Strong Excel or spreadsheet skills
Excellent organizational skills and attention to detail
Ability to manage multiple projects, deadlines, and financial priorities simultaneously
Strong written and verbal communication skills
Comfortable communicating directly with clients regarding invoices and collections
Experience with WIP reporting and construction financial reporting is highly preferred

Preferred Experience

Commercial construction or subcontractor accounting
AIA/progress billing
Change order tracking
Certified payroll
Construction ERP or project management software

new_jobs.title: Controlling Professional
new_jobs.description:
Cómo será tu día

Como Factory Controller, trabajarás en el análisis, control y seguimiento de los costos de la fábrica, asegurando una lectura clara de los principales drivers del negocio y la correcta aplicación de los métodos de costeo definidos por la compañía. Tendrás una interacción constante con áreas operativas, financieras y de soporte para controlar costos fijos y variables, inventarios, CAPEX, rentabilidad por línea y procesos de cierre. Será una posición clave para generar visibilidad financiera, anticipar desviaciones y apoyar decisiones que impactan la eficiencia, competitividad y sostenibilidad de la operación.

Cuál es tu responsabilidad

Proyectar y controlar los principales elementos de la estructura de costos de la entidad, incluyendo costos administrativos, de producción y bases para el costeo estándar.
Controlar las notificaciones de producción, especialmente en procesos de metalmecánica, definiendo costos estándar y monitoreando over / under absorption.
Asegurar que las órdenes de fabricación sean notificadas y cerradas oportunamente para garantizar registros contables correctos durante el cierre comercial.
Preparar forecast de fábrica con base en pronósticos de notificaciones, evolución de costos, centros de costo y líneas de producto.
Mantener actualizados los precios estándar y estructuras de costos para asegurar tarifas de venta consistentes y confiables para los clientes.
Analizar variaciones en Change in Inventories, movimientos contables en SAP y transacciones de órdenes de producción para anticipar impactos financieros.
Identificar y analizar la rentabilidad por línea de producto, examinando movimientos atípicos y variaciones relevantes en profit.
Planificar, monitorear y controlar costos fijos e indirectos de fábrica, incluyendo license fees, infra costs y otros acuerdos con terceros o compañías asociadas.
Gestionar y controlar inversiones CAPEX de acuerdo con lineamientos corporativos y necesidades operativas, incluyendo control de activos, registro contable y coordinación con tesorería.
Analizar costos de no conformidad, provisiones, inventarios, costos y activos, preparando conciliaciones e informes confiables para stakeholders internos.
Cumplir y promover lineamientos de calidad, EHS y seguridad física aplicables al rol, escalando desviaciones críticas y soportando una operación segura y controlada.

Cuáles son los requisitos para el cargo

Profesional en Contabilidad, Finanzas, Ingenierías, Administración de Empresas o áreas afines; deseable especialización o certificaciones en costos, finanzas, controlling o campos relacionados.
Más de 2 años de experiencia en áreas de control de negocio, control de costos, controlling financiero o roles similares; deseable experiencia en procesos productivos o industriales.
Conocimientos en métodos de costeo, contabilidad, costos estándar, inventarios, CAPEX, provisiones, cierre financiero y análisis de rentabilidad.
Manejo de SAP y herramientas Microsoft Office, especialmente Excel; deseable experiencia con Power BI, Tableau o Alteryx para análisis y visualización de información.
Inglés intermedio.
Competencias: orientación al resultado, pensamiento analítico, criterio financiero, colaboración, comunicación efectiva, autonomía, proactividad y capacidad para trabajar con equipos multifuncionales.

Acerca del equipo

Formarás parte del equipo de Performance & Factory Controlling de la fábrica de transformadores ubicada en Tenjo, Cundinamarca. Este equipo es responsable de la planificación, análisis y control financiero de la operación, asegurando que la organización cuente con información precisa y oportuna para cumplir sus objetivos estratégicos y operativos.

El equipo de Controlling se enfoca en el análisis de costos, presupuestos, pronósticos, productividad, indicadores clave de rendimiento y mejora continua de procesos. Trabajamos de manera cercana con producción, supply chain, contabilidad, compras, proyectos y otras áreas del negocio para fortalecer la toma de decisiones y contribuir a una operación más eficiente y competitiva.

¿Qué es Siemens Energy?

En Siemens Energy somos más que una empresa de tecnología energética. Satisfacemos la creciente demanda de energía en más de 90 países, al mismo tiempo que garantizamos la protección de nuestro clima. Con más de 92 000 empleados, no solo generamos electricidad para más del 16 % de la comunidad mundial, sino que también usamos nuestra tecnología para ayudar a proteger a las personas y al medio ambiente.

Nuestro equipo global está comprometido a hacer realidad la energía sostenible, fiable y asequible al ampliar los límites de lo que es posible. Mantenemos un legado de innovación de 150 años que fomenta nuestra búsqueda de personas que respalden nuestro enfoque en la descarbonización, las nuevas tecnologías y la transformación energética.

Nuestro compromiso con la diversidad

Job Description

As a Senior Accountant, you will maintain financial records and ensure that financial transactions are properly recorded. You will maintain the accuracy of entries to ledger accounts and reconcile subsidiary ledger accounts to the general ledger. You will prepare complex balance sheets, profit and loss statements and other financial reports. You will analyze current costs, revenues, financial commitments, and obligations incurred to predict future revenues and expenses. You may guide lower-level accountants.

Responsibilities

Prepares journal entries, analyzes accounts, prepares statements, and assists accounting manager with monthly closing and accounting reports.
Compiles and analyzes financial information to prepare entries for accounts, including general ledger and document business transactions.
Maintains and coordinates implementation of accounting and control procedures.
Resolves and corrects billing, inventory, costing, and other accounting discrepancies.
Prepares documentation of processes and procedures and recommends improvements.
Prepares general ledger account reconciliations.
Researches and explains general ledger account variances to trend, budget, and prior year.
Monitors and reviews accounting and related systems’ reports for accuracy and completeness.
Prepares and reviews budget, revenue, expense, payroll entries, invoices, and other accounting documents.
Analyzes revenue and expenditure trends and recommends appropriate budget levels, and ensures expenditure control.
Explains accounting policies to staff.
Recommends, develops, and maintains financial databases, software, and manual filing systems.
Supervises input and handling of financial data and reports for company automated financial systems.
Interacts with internal and external auditors in completing audits.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance or related field required
CIMA/ACA/ACCA/ICAEW/CPA qualified preferred
3 years required, 5 years preferred, of accounting experience
Accounting theory, and application of principles and practices
Principles and practices of financial record keeping and reporting
Analysis and interpretation of complex financial and statistical data
Assembly and preparation of data for reports
Strong office and computer skills
Strong written and verbal communication skills
Able to prepare, examine, and verify financial reports

Able to research and analyze varieties of information

About WPP Media

WPP is the trusted growth partner for the world’s leading brands. With exceptional talent, trusted data and intelligence, and world-class partnerships – all united by our pioneering agentic marketing platform, WPP Open – we help clients navigate change, capture opportunity, and deliver transformational growth. 

WPP Media is WPP's AI-driven media operating unit, bringing together media, data, and partnerships to deliver creative personalisation at scale. Connected through WPP Open and powered by Open Intelligence, clients see exactly where, how, and why their media investment is working.

For more information, visit wppmedia.com.

Role Summary and Impact

As part of the Global Operations Centre (GOC), you will work closely with teams across the United States, Europe, and Asia to deliver high-impact solutions in a collaborative, multicultural environment. We are looking for a Business Operations Specialist – Cloud
who will drive cloud financial management, cost analysis, and optimization across the Media cluster, supporting FinOps delivery in close partnership with Finance and Technology teams.

Key Responsibilities

FinOps Delivery Support & Media Cluster Partnership: Work in close partnership with the central FinOps team to support FinOps activities related to the Media cluster. Provide Finance execution support where capacity is constrained and act as a consistent Finance point-of-contact for Media cloud cost topics.
Cloud Spend Analysis & Financial Insight: Analyse Media cloud spend to identify key cost drivers, trends, and variances. Support the improvement of cost attribution (e.g., allocation, tagging quality, cost centre alignment) to increase transparency and translate cloud cost data into clear financial insights for Finance and Technology stakeholders.
Cloud Cost Optimisation Support: Collaborate with FinOps, Tech Ops, and Global Product teams to identify and validate cloud cost optimisation opportunities. Assist in defining baselines, estimating savings, tracking delivery, and maintaining visibility of optimisation activities, risks, and realised benefits.
Forecasting, Budgeting & Actuals Support: Support budgeting, forecasting, and actuals variance tracking for Media cloud spend, ensuring accurate alignment between operational consumption and financial planning.
Reporting, Governance & Continuous Improvement: Support the production of consistent, Finance-quality reporting and showback information for Media stakeholders. Ensure appropriate documentation and audit trails in line with WPP Finance policies, while contributing to the refinement of FinOps trackers, templates, and ways of working between Finance, FinOps, and Technology teams.

Skills And Experience

If this opportunity looks right for you, we are looking for candidates who have:

3+ years of experience in IT Finance or Tech Finance as a Financial Analyst with strong skills in cost analysis, modeling,variance explanation and IT Budgeting experience is a MUST.
Bachelor's degree is a must
Advanced English level (Written & speaking) (this will be assess during the interview process)
Advanced Excel proficiency (VLOOKUPs, pivot tables, complex data analysis); exposure to Microsoft Copilot or AI tools is a plus.
Experience with ERPs and CRMS.
Understanding of Cloud costs & FinOps concepts (or a strong learning mindset) to analyze consumption-based spend, challenge data, and identify savings.
Experience in large, complex matrix organizations or global tech/services companies, collaborating across international regions.
Self-driven & proactive mindset with the ability to work independently, reach out to stakeholders to ask the right questions, and bring structure to financial data.

Life at WPP Media & Benefits

Life At WPP Media & Benefits

Our passion for shaping the next era of media is powered by our commitment to Be Extraordinary, investing in our employees to inspire transformational creativity. We also Lead Optimistically, firmly believing in and Championing Growth and Development for every individual. This commitment allows WPP Media employees to leverage the extensive global WPP Media & WPP networks to pursue their passions, build vital professional connections, and learn at the cutting edge of marketing and advertising.

We Create an Open environment built on trust and respect, where everyone feels they belong and has opportunities to progress. Our comprehensive benefits package reflects this commitment, including competitive medical, group retirement plans, vision, and dental insurance, significant paid time off, preferential partner discounts, and employee mental health awareness days.

Role Summary and Impact

As part of the Global Operations Centre (GOC), you will work closely with teams across the United States, Europe, and Asia to deliver high-impact solutions in a collaborative, multicultural environment. We are looking for a Business Operations Specialist – Cloud
who will drive cloud financial management, cost analysis, and optimization across the Media cluster, supporting FinOps delivery in close partnership with Finance and Technology teams.

Key Responsibilities

FinOps Delivery Support & Media Cluster Partnership: Work in close partnership with the central FinOps team to support FinOps activities related to the Media cluster. Provide Finance execution support where capacity is constrained and act as a consistent Finance point-of-contact for Media cloud cost topics.
Cloud Spend Analysis & Financial Insight: Analyse Media cloud spend to identify key cost drivers, trends, and variances. Support the improvement of cost attribution (e.g., allocation, tagging quality, cost centre alignment) to increase transparency and translate cloud cost data into clear financial insights for Finance and Technology stakeholders.
Cloud Cost Optimisation Support: Collaborate with FinOps, Tech Ops, and Global Product teams to identify and validate cloud cost optimisation opportunities. Assist in defining baselines, estimating savings, tracking delivery, and maintaining visibility of optimisation activities, risks, and realised benefits.
Forecasting, Budgeting & Actuals Support: Support budgeting, forecasting, and actuals variance tracking for Media cloud spend, ensuring accurate alignment between operational consumption and financial planning.
Reporting, Governance & Continuous Improvement: Support the production of consistent, Finance-quality reporting and showback information for Media stakeholders. Ensure appropriate documentation and audit trails in line with WPP Finance policies, while contributing to the refinement of FinOps trackers, templates, and ways of working between Finance, FinOps, and Technology teams.

Skills And Experience

If this opportunity looks right for you, we are looking for candidates who have:

3+ years of experience in IT Finance or Tech Finance as a Financial Analyst with strong skills in cost analysis, modeling,variance explanation and IT Budgeting experience is a MUST.
Bachelor's degree is a must
Advanced English level (Written & speaking) (this will be assess during the interview process)
Advanced Excel proficiency (VLOOKUPs, pivot tables, complex data analysis); exposure to Microsoft Copilot or AI tools is a plus.
Experience with ERPs and CRMS.
Understanding of Cloud costs & FinOps concepts (or a strong learning mindset) to analyze consumption-based spend, challenge data, and identify savings.
Experience in large, complex matrix organizations or global tech/services companies, collaborating across international regions.
Self-driven & proactive mindset with the ability to work independently, reach out to stakeholders to ask the right questions, and bring structure to financial data.
